digest.component_or_area: rebar CLI commands (comment, create, edit, session-log, tag, untag, archive)
propositions: The rebar command accepts flag-like tokens (e.g. --body-file, --body) as positional body arguments, storing the flag name as the comment text and silently discarding the intended content, while exiting with code 0.
Surplus positional arguments containing the actual intended body value are dropped by an args[:min_args] slice, compounding silent data loss.
Users expecting a --body-file or --body option reach for these non-existent flags, losing critical work like root-cause analysis, fix rationale, and audit trails to the live store.
The failure mode is undetectable at write time because the command exits 0, a comment object is created, and len(comments) checks pass despite missing content.
A guard clause must reject body arguments beginning with - and must provide a -- escape hatch for legitimate dash-prefixed content across all positional-body commands.
The same footgun affects multiple commands (comment, create, edit, session-log, tag, untag, archive) and must be fixed uniformly via a command-table-driven guard.
